messages.subject: Grouping Time Structure
parts:
Hello all,

I am constructing a model for an hourly time series data using AR(1) processes for every day throughout the course of the year. I would like to group my data by day and then see how the rho parameters for each day are correlated. Am I correct in using the following to do this?

formula <- y ~ f(time.hour, model = "ar1",
                 group = time.day, control.group = list(model = "ar1"))

mod <- inla(formula, data = data, family = "gaussian")

Can I then interpret the groupRho parameters as the parameter for how my rho for each day changes over time?

Thanks,
Eric

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Grouping Time Structure
parts:
Hi,
The group rho in that model should tell you how similar the daily hourly cycle is from day to day; a value close to 1 would mean that the cycle changes slowly over the year.
The hourly process rho will model how variable the cycle is within the day.

The group rho does not however say how the rho for the hourly process changes over time, since both rho parameters are global; they are fixed over time. Only the process itself changes from day to day, not its dependence parameters.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Grouping Time Structure
parts:
Hi,

Varying rho across the year (with a process model for rho itself) doesn’t fall under the latent Gaussian framework that inla handles; only a single layer of latent Gaussian can be present. The parameters of those Gaussians need in practice have low (ca 5-15) total dimension, and 365 is quite a lot in that context.  However, if you restrict rho to vary only slowly over the year (e.g. with logit(rho) the weighted sum of a few harmonic functions), there may be a way to achieve what you’re looking for,
by using the inla rgeneric framework, that allows you to define arbitrary precision models in R code. With that, you can define a joint model for all your daily time series, with a few parameters defining the block-diagonal precision matrix  Look for examples of rgeneric on the r-inla.org site.

Finn
